title: Data Skew Mitigation: Account Skew and Lookup Lock Contention

steps.prompt: Over 80,000 Contact records are assigned to a single "Unassigned Holding Account". When integration jobs insert contacts concurrently, transactions fail with UNABLE_TO_LOCK_ROW. What architectural pattern mitigates this Account Skew?

options.label: Distribute child contacts round-robin across a dedicated pool of parent holding Accounts
options.rationale: Distributing child records across a pool of parent accounts diffuses lock contention across distinct database rows, eliminating locking serialization bottlenecks.

options.label: Enable Granular Locking on the org and assign the holding account to a top-level user role
options.distractorAntipattern: Granular locking optimizes sharing recalculations, not transactional parent row locks during child DML.
options.rationale: Granular locking helps prevent group maintenance conflicts during role hierarchy changes, but does not prevent row-level locking on parent records during child inserts.

options.label: Convert Account lookup fields on Contact to non-clearing lookups without parent validation
options.distractorAntipattern: Standard contact-account relationships inherently lock parent rows regardless of custom lookup configurations.
options.rationale: Standard parent-child relationships always acquire an exclusive row lock on the parent record during child DML to maintain referential integrity.
